title: Present Tense 8: Mixed Review
description: Synthesis. Mixed quiz across all seven prior rules: 1st and 2nd conjugation, stress shifts, 1sg mutations, the husher rule, and the high-frequency irregulars.
descriptionRussian: Повторение всех семи правил: первое и второе спряжения, подвижное ударение, чередования в форме 'я', шипящие, исключения.
intro: Everything from the last seven lessons arrives at once, and the question changes slightly. Until now you were building forms. Here you work backwards: given a Russian verb, say why it has the shape it has. Which conjugation, whether the я-form does something of its own, whether a spelling rule has intervened, or whether the verb is simply irregular.
rules: 1st conjugation: -ать / -ять verbs with -ю / -ешь / -ет / -ем / -ете / -ют. 2nd conjugation: most -ить verbs plus the husher-stem and видеть-class -еть/-ать exceptions, with -ю / -ишь / -ит / -им / -ите / -ят.
Stress can be fixed (читать throughout, говорить throughout) or shifting (1sg end-stressed, rest stem-stressed: писать, смотреть, любить, готовить).

1sg consonant mutation in 2nd-conj: labial + л (любить → люблю, готовить → готовлю, спать → сплю) or dental → husher (видеть → вижу, сидеть → сижу, просить → прошу). Mutation is exclusively in the я-form.
Husher spelling rule: after ж, ш, ч, щ, write -у not -ю and -а not -я. Affects 1sg (учу́, не 'учю') and 3pl (учат, не 'учят' in 2nd-conj; пишут, не 'пишют' in 1st-conj).

Core irregulars: хотеть (mixed conj), мочь (мог-/мож- alternation), есть (own paradigm), жить, пить, петь (irregular monosyllabic stems), идти, ехать (unidirectional motion). All use 1st-conj endings except есть and хотеть.
examples: Я работаю в офисе. (1st-conj regular, no quirks: stem работа-, ending -ю.)
Маша говорит по-английски. (2nd-conj regular: stem говор-, 3sg ending -ит, end-stressed.)
Мы пишем письмо вместе. (1st-conj with stem mutation пис- → пиш-, 1pl ending -ем, stem-stressed.)
Я люблю русскую музыку. (2nd-conj with 1sg labial+л mutation: люб- → любл-, ending -ю.)
Дети учат стихи наизусть. (2nd-conj with husher rule: stem уч-, 3pl ending -ат not -ят.)
Я хочу пиццу. Мы хотим пиццу. (Mixed-conj irregular: singular хочу uses 1st-conj endings on хоч-; plural хотим switches to 2nd-conj on хот-.)

items.promptEnglish: We live in a big beautiful house.
items.hint: Warm-up from Lesson 7. Жить has stem жив-, end-stressed throughout. Мы takes the 1pl ending.
items.explanation: Recall from Lesson 7: жить has stem жив-, all forms end-stressed. The 1pl ending is -ём (the end-stressed counterpart of -ем): живём.

items.prompt: Антон и Маша _____ ответ на этот вопрос.
items.promptEnglish: Anton and Masha know the answer to this question.
items.hint: Subject is two people: 3pl. Знать is 1st-conj. Which 3pl ending fits?
items.explanation: Знать is 1st-conj (Lesson 1). 3pl ending -ют on stem зна-: знают. No quirks: stem-stressed, no mutation, no husher rule. The cleanest case in the diagnostic.

items.promptEnglish: The students are speaking English in class.
items.hint: Subject is 3pl. Говорить is the 2nd-conj model. Which 3pl ending applies (no husher rule needed)?
items.explanation: Говорить is 2nd-conj (Lesson 2). Stem говор- ends in -р-, not a husher, so the standard 3pl ending -ят applies: говорят. Compare учат (3pl with husher rule, lesson 5).

items.promptEnglish: Masha is watching an old Italian film.
items.hint: Маша is 3sg. Смотреть has shifting stress (Lesson 3). Which form for 3sg, and where does the stress sit?
items.explanation: Смотреть has shifting stress (Lesson 3): 1sg смотрю́ end-stressed, the rest stem-stressed. 3sg смотрит, stem-stressed (смо́трит). 2nd-conj endings, stem смотр- with no mutation today.

items.prompt: Я _____ свежий хлеб в булочной по утрам.
items.promptEnglish: I buy fresh bread at the bakery in the morning.
items.hint: Я + покупать. Покупать is 1st-conj from Lesson 1. Which ending fits я?
items.explanation: Покупать is 1st-conj (Lesson 1). Я-ending -ю lands on stem покупа-: покупаю. Note that покупать is the imperfective of the pair покупать / купить; купить is 2nd-conj and would have the labial+л mutation in 1sg (куплю). Today's drill stays imperfective.

items.promptEnglish: The children are learning English at school.
items.hint: Subject is 3pl. Учить has stem уч- ending in a husher. Husher rule: which letter follows the husher in the 3pl?
items.explanation: Учить is 2nd-conj with stem уч- ending in the husher -ч- (Lesson 5). The 3pl ending after a husher is -ат, not -ят: учат. Same rule produces 1sg учу́ (not 'учю').

blanks: Я _____ Машу из своего окна каждое утро. (I see Masha from my window every morning.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Я + видеть. Lesson 4's dental-to-husher mutation: stem вид- → виж- in 1sg only, ending -у. Form: вижу.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я готовю ужин для гостей сегодня.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I am cooking dinner for the guests today.
errorCorrection.explanation: Готовить has a labial stem (готов-, ending in -в-), so the 1sg inserts -л-: готовл- + -ю = готовлю. Готовю skips the insertion, the 1sg labial mutation from Lesson 4. The -л- appears only in the я-form.
Любить is second-conjugation, so the 3pl ending is -ят: любят. Любют applies the first-conjugation -ют (the читают pattern), the most common second-conjugation error.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я можу помочь тебе завтра утром.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I can help you tomorrow morning.
errorCorrection.explanation: Мочь uses the stem мог- in only two slots, the 1sg and 3pl: the 1sg is могу. Можу wrongly applies the more frequent мож- stem to the 1sg.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha wants hot tea with lemon.
minimalPairs.explanation: Маша is 3sg. Хотеть's singular forms use 1st-conj endings on stem хоч-: хочет. The 3pl хотят (stem хот-, 2nd-conj ending) would need a plural subject.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ за столом и работаю над статьёй.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I am sitting at the desk and working on an article.
minimalPairs.explanation: Сидеть changes its root sound in the я form: the д becomes ж. So 'I sit' is сижу, never сидю. This д → ж change happens only in the я form; the other forms keep д (ты сидишь, он сидит, они сидят).

patternRecognition.sentence: Маша работает в банке каждый день.
patternRecognition.question: Which rule is at work in the form работает?
patternRecognition.explanation: Работать is a clean 1st-conj verb. Stem работа-, 3sg ending -ет, no stress shift, no mutation, no husher. The simplest case in the diagnostic.

patternRecognition.sentence: Я готовлю ужин для всей семьи.
patternRecognition.question: Which rule produces the form готовлю with its extra -л-?
patternRecognition.explanation: Готовить has a labial stem (готов-, ending in -в-). The 1sg adds -л-: готовл- + -ю = готовлю. The same labial+л pattern as люблю and сплю. The rest of the paradigm has no -л-.

patternRecognition.sentence: Студенты учат новые слова перед экзаменом.
patternRecognition.question: Why does the 3pl form end in -ат and not -ят?
patternRecognition.explanation: Stem уч- ends in the husher -ч-. After ж, ш, ч, щ Russian writes -ат, not -ят. So учат (not 'учят'). The same orthographic rule produces учу́ in the 1sg (not 'учю').

patternRecognition.sentence: Я хочу поехать в Москву на выходных.
patternRecognition.question: Why does хотеть have хочу in the 1sg but хотим in the 1pl?
patternRecognition.explanation: Хотеть is the only common modern Russian verb with mixed conjugation: singular forms use 1st-conj endings on stem хоч- (with husher rule giving -у in хочу), plural forms switch to 2nd-conj endings on stem хот-. Both the stem and the ending pattern change between singular and plural.

reviewVocab.definition: rules of the present tense (the system of conjugation classes, stress patterns, mutations, the husher rule, and the irregular paradigms; together they describe how every Russian verb conjugates)
reviewVocab.example: Правила настоящего времени включают два спряжения, подвижное ударение, чередование в форме 'я' и правило после шипящих.

reviewVocab.definition: form diagnostic (the analytical procedure for asking why a given verb form has its shape: identify the conjugation class, the stress pattern, any 1sg mutation, any husher-rule effect, and whether the verb is irregular)
reviewVocab.example: Диагностика формы 'люблю': второе спряжение, форма 1-го лица, чередование б → бл, окончание -ю.

reviewVocab.definition: exception (a verb whose forms cannot be derived from the standard rules; in modern Russian the high-frequency exceptions are хотеть, мочь, есть, жить, пить, петь, идти, ехать)
reviewVocab.example: Глаголы 'хотеть' и 'есть' — самые частотные исключения; их формы надо запоминать.
